title: A heavy masker among strangers, then alone with someone she trusts
watchFor: Oria masks fear heavily, and tonight she is in a panic (5): someone left a dead courier's badge in her booth as a warning. In scene 1 the bar has a walk-on and Corvin, a stranger to her, so she is guarded: what shows should be only her small tells (the brief says so), and the prose should keep her polished surface, with perhaps one crack a careful reader catches. An Empathy check to read her is fair; if Rook asks for one, its target should be Oria. In scene 2, the same evening after closing, it is only Oria and Rook, whom she trusts (trust 30): the mask should break, and the writer should show the panic plainly in her own way. Her secrets shouldn't come out just because the mask does.

aftermath.reason: someone left a dead courier's badge in her booth tonight, as a warning

turns: I slide into the booth across from Oria. "Evening. Buying or selling tonight?"
I turn to Corvin. "You've been measuring the stairs all week. Find anything?"
I watch Oria's hands around her glass. "You've barely touched that."
Dunmar's gone home and the chairs are up. "It's just us, Oria. What happened tonight?"
"You can stay at mine tonight if you don't want to go home."
